pr.title: Let InstCombine remove Clone shims inside Clone shims
pr.description:
The Clone shims that we generate tend to recurse into other Clone shims, which gets very silly very quickly. Here's our current state: https://godbolt.org/z/E69YeY8eq

So I've added InstSimplify to the shims optimization passes, and improved `is_trivially_pure_clone_copy` so that it can delete those calls inside the shim. This makes the shim way smaller because most of its size is the required ceremony for unwinding.

This change also completely breaks the UI test added for https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/104870. With this PR, that program ICEs in MIR type checking because `is_trivially_pure_clone_copy` and the trait solver disagree on whether `*mut u8` is `Copy`. And adding the requisite `Copy` impl to make them agree makes the test not generate any diagnostics. Considering that I spent most of my time on this PR fixing `#![no_core]` tests, I would prefer to just delete this one. The maintenance burden of `#![no_core]` is uniquely high because when they break they tend to break in very confusing ways.

classification.name: InstSimplify
evidence: The PR’s reusable MIR transformation knowledge is in InstSimplify: it adds InstSimplify to the shim optimization pipeline, and broadens is_trivially_pure_clone_copy so the existing simplify_primitive_clone peephole can remove nested Clone shim calls for raw pointers and shared references. The helper change itself is not a separate pass; the tests and lang-item additions support this optimization.

processing.reason: The PR is explicitly an optimization, not a semantic correction. Its only compiler behavior changes are (1) adding `InstSimplify` to the shim pass pipeline and (2) broadening `is_trivially_pure_clone_copy` so shared references and raw pointers are treated as trivially pure clone/copy. Both the old conservative behavior (retain nested member `Clone` shim calls) and the new behavior (delete them) compute exactly the same value: shared-reference and raw-pointer `Clone` is a value-preserving copy, and trivially pure members have no observable side effects by construction. The supplied regression test asserts only that inner `call <i32 as Clone>::clone`/`call <*const i32 as Clone>::clone` instructions disappear; it makes no runtime-value claim. The PR's possible ICE for a `#![no_core]` test is a historical compile-time type-checking failure caused by disagreement with the trait solver, not a runtime differing-value transformation, and cannot be encoded as two ordinary Rust functions producing different deterministic numeric/boolean/character results under the fixed modern compiler. Consequently there is no source-grounded ORIGINAL-vs-INCORRECT function pair with different observable return values, and manufacturing one (e.g., unsafely dropping a `Clone` call for a non-Copy mutable-reference member, which the PR explicitly keeps false) would invent a transformation the patch never made.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this optimization PR, `is_trivially_pure_clone_copy` deliberately classified non-mutable shared references and raw pointers as not trivially pure clone/copy: `ty::Ref(_, _, hir::Mutability::Not) | ty::RawPtr(..) => false`, with the comment `Thin pointers & thin shared references are pure-clone-copy, but for anything with custom metadata it might be more complicated.` The shim optimization pipeline also omitted `InstSimplify`. Consequently, compiler-generated aggregate `Clone` shims retained calls to member `Clone` shims even when those members were shared references or raw pointers.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: This is an optimization PR, not a semantic bug fix: the historical behavior was an over-conservative no-op, not a miscompile. The prior transformation kept nested member `Clone` shim calls inside the aggregate `Clone` shim when a member was a shared reference or raw pointer. The corrected transformation classifies non-mutable shared references and raw pointers as trivially pure clone/copy and runs `InstSimplify` in the shim pipeline so those inner calls are deleted. A comparison should therefore vary presence/absence of that simplification, not invent an unsafe "remove too much" rewrite; mutable references remain classified false (`ty::Ref(_, _, hir::Mutability::Mut) => false`).
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies of compiler-generated `Clone` shims for aggregates whose members are trivially pure clone/copy, especially aggregates containing `i32`, non-mutable shared references, or raw pointers such as `(i32, i32, *const i32)`. The relevant IR shape is an aggregate `Clone` shim that calls the `Clone` shims of its members. The supplied regression test targets codegen with `pub type Test = (i32, i32, *const i32);` and `<Test as core::clone::Clone>::clone`, compiled without MIR inlining.
analysis.summary: For compiler-generated aggregate `Clone` shims, add `InstSimplify` to the shim optimization pipeline and broaden `is_trivially_pure_clone_copy` to accept non-mutable shared references and raw pointers, allowing `simplify_primitive_clone` to remove nested member `Clone` calls without relying on MIR inlining. This is an optimization; mutable references remain non-trivial.
analysis.trigger: A `Clone` shim is generated for an aggregate whose members are trivially pure clone/copy, including non-mutable shared references or raw pointers, and the shim pipeline reaches `InstSimplify` after `SimplifyCfg::MakeShim`. The shim initially contains calls to member `Clone` shims that can be replaced/removed.
preconditions: `InstSimplify` is included in the shim optimization pass list, as shown by `&instsimplify::InstSimplify,` adjacent to `&simplify::SimplifyCfg::MakeShim,`.
The member type is classified trivially pure clone/copy; for this change `ty::Ref(_, _, hir::Mutability::Not) | ty::RawPtr(..) => true`.
The member is not a mutable reference, which remains `ty::Ref(_, _, hir::Mutability::Mut) => false`.
The optimization must not depend on MIR inlining; the regression test disables it with `-Zinline-mir=no`.
pitfalls: Do not describe this as a confirmed runtime bug fix: the patch is explicitly about reducing unnecessary shim/IR size, and no execution or reproduction was performed.
Do not generalize the classification change to mutable references; the patch retains `ty::Ref(_, _, hir::Mutability::Mut) => false`.

The helper and trait solver must agree on `Copy`. The PR description states that a `#![no_core]` test ICEs in MIR type checking because `is_trivially_pure_clone_copy` and the trait solver disagree on whether `*mut u8` is `Copy`.

When using `no_core`/lang-item tests, matching `Copy` impls may be required; the patch adds `impl<T: ?Sized> Copy for *mut T {}` to `rsbegin.rs`/`rsend.rs` and pointer/reference impls to affected tests.
Do not infer the optimization from ordinary MIR inlining; the supplied test explicitly disables inlining and checks that inner calls are gone anyway.
analysis.testStrategy: Use a focused codegen regression test for a compiler-generated aggregate `Clone` shim. The supplied test uses `pub type Test = (i32, i32, *const i32);` and `pub static TEST: fn(&Test) -> Test = <Test as core::clone::Clone>::clone;`, with flags `-Cno-prepopulate-passes -Csymbol-mangling-version=v0 -Zinline-mir=no`, then asserts no calls remain to member shims: `CHECK-NOT: call <i32 as core::clone::Clone>::clone` and `CHECK-NOT: call <*const i32 as core::clone::Clone>::clone`, while checking the aggregate shim symbol is present. To isolate the transformation, compare the same aggregate Clone shim with `InstSimplify` enabled/instsimplifyable member classification versus the prior conservative behavior; the corrected IR should omit inner member `Clone` calls without inlining. Include a mutable-reference member as a control that should not be treated as trivially pure clone/copy if testing the classification boundary.
